exampleAnswers.title: Finding an Expression for a Least-Squares Regression Curve

question.text:
$x$ $0$ $1$ $2$ $3$ $4$
$y$ $-4$ $-5$ $2$ $-1$ $-3$

Consider the data above and the matrices below. Find an expression for the vector of coefficients of the curve $y=\beta_0 + \beta_1 x + \beta_2 x^2 + \beta_3 x^3$ that best fits the data.

\[ X = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0^2 & 0^3 \\ 1 & 1 & 1^2 & 1^3 \\ 1 & 2 & 2^2 & 2^3 \\ 1 & 3 & 3^2 & 3^3 \\ 1 & 4 & 4^2 & 4^3 \end{bmatrix}, \qquad \boldsymbol{\beta} = \begin{bmatrix} \beta_0 \\ \beta_1 \\ \beta_2 \\ \beta_3 \\ \end{bmatrix}, \qquad \mathbf{y} = \begin{bmatrix} -4 \\ -5 \\ 2 \\ -1 \\ -3 \end{bmatrix} \]
question.explanation:
The coefficients of the curve

\[ y=\beta_0 + \beta_1 x + \beta_2 x^2 + \beta_3 x^3 \]

that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution ${\hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}}$ to the system

\[ X \boldsymbol{\beta} = \mathbf{y}, \]

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\boldsymbol{\beta}$ is the parameter vector, and $\mathbf{y}$ is the observation vector.

Pre-multiplying this equation by $X^T,$ we obtain the corresponding normal equation

\[ X^T \! X {\hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}} = X^T \mathbf{y}. \]

Since the columns of $X$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${X^T}X$ is invertible and

\[ {\hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}} = (X^T \! X )^{-1} X^T \mathbf{y}. \]

exampleAnswers.title: Identifying the Elements of a Polynomial Regression Model

question.text:
$x$ $1$ $3$ $5$ $7$ $9$
$y$ $-1$ $-5$ $-3$ $-4$ $5$

The vector of coefficients of the curve $y=\beta_0 + \beta_1 x + \beta_2 x^2 + \beta_3 x^3$ that best fits the data above can be found using polynomial regression as

\[ \begin{bmatrix} \beta_0 \\ \beta_1 \\ \beta_2 \\ \beta_3 \end{bmatrix} = (X^T \! X)^{-1} X^T \mathbf{y}, \]

where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $\mathbf{y}$ is the observation vector. Which of the following is the design matrix $X$ in this context?
question.explanation:
$x$ $\color{blue}1$ $\color{blue}3$ $\color{blue}5$ $\color{blue}7$ $\color{blue}9$
$y$ $\color{red}-1$ $\color{red}-5$ $\color{red}-3$ $\color{red}-4$ $\color{red}5$

The coefficients of the curve

\[ y=\beta_0 + \beta_1 x + \beta_2 x^2 + \beta_3 x^3 \]

that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution ${\hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}}$ to the system

\begin{align*} \overbrace{ \begin{bmatrix} 1 & \color{blue}1 & \color{blue}1^2 & \color{blue}1^3 \\ 1 & \color{blue}3 & \color{blue}3^2 & \color{blue}3^3 \\ 1 & \color{blue}5 & \color{blue}5^2 & \color{blue}5^3 \\ 1 & \color{blue}7 & \color{blue}7^2 & \color{blue}7^3 \\ 1 & \color{blue}9 & \color{blue}9^2 & \color{blue}9^3 \end{bmatrix} }^{X} \overbrace{ \begin{bmatrix} \beta_0 \\ \beta_1 \\ \beta_2 \\ \beta_3 \end{bmatrix} }^{ \boldsymbol{\beta}} &= \overbrace{ \begin{bmatrix} \color{red}-1 \\ \color{red}-5 \\ \color{red}-3 \\ \color{red}-4 \\ \color{red}5 \end{bmatrix} }^{ \mathbf{y}}, \end{align*}

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\boldsymbol{\beta}$ is the parameter vector, and $\mathbf{y}$ is the observation vector.

\begin{align*} \overbrace{ \begin{bmatrix} \color{blue}1 & \color{blue}1^2 & \color{blue}1^3 \\ \color{blue}3 & \color{blue}3^2 & \color{blue}3^3 \\ \color{blue}5 & \color{blue}5^2 & \color{blue}5^3 \\ \color{blue}7 & \color{blue}7^2 & \color{blue}7^3 \\ \color{blue}9 & \color{blue}9^2 & \color{blue}9^3 \end{bmatrix} }^{X} \overbrace{ \begin{bmatrix} \beta_1 \\ \beta_2 \\ \beta_3 \end{bmatrix} }^{ \boldsymbol{\beta}} &= \overbrace{ \begin{bmatrix} \color{red}-5 \\ \color{red}0 \\ \color{red}-1 \\ \color{red}2 \\ \color{red}-1 \end{bmatrix} }^{ \mathbf{y}}, \end{align*}

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\boldsymbol{\beta}$ is the parameter vector, and $\mathbf{y}$ is the observation vector.

example.title: Identifying the Design Matrix When the Regression Curve Contains Zero Coefficients
